sanskrit: taṃ prapadya sadā vatsa sarvabhāvena śaṃkaram tatprasādāc ca kāmebhyaḥ phalaṃ prāpsyasi putraka
english: Take refuge always in Śaṃkara, my child, with your whole being; by his grace, little son, you shall win from your desires their fruit.

sanskrit: jananyās tad vacaḥ śrutvā tadāprabhṛti śatruhan mama bhaktir mahādeve naiṣṭhikī samapadyata
english: Having heard those words of my mother, O slayer of foes, from that day onward an unwavering devotion to Mahādeva took root in me.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tapa āsthāya toṣayām āsa śaṃkaram divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu pādāṅguṣṭhāgraviṣṭhitaḥ
english: Then, undertaking austerity, I set myself to please Śaṃkara, standing for a thousand divine years poised upon the tips of my toes.

sanskrit: ekaṃ varṣaśataṃ caiva phalāhāras tadābhavam dvitīyaṃ śīrṇaparṇāśī tṛtīyaṃ cāmbubhojanaḥ śatāni sapta caivāhaṃ vāyubhakṣas tadābhavam
english: For one hundred years I lived then on fruit alone; for a second hundred I ate withered leaves; for a third I subsisted on water; and for seven hundred years more I fed upon air alone.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ sarvalokeśvaraḥ prabhuḥ śakrarūpaṃ sa kṛtvā tu sarvair devagaṇair vṛtaḥ sahasrākṣas tadā bhūtvā vajrapāṇir mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then Mahādeva, the Lord and Master of all worlds, was pleased; assuming the form of Śakra and encircled by all the hosts of the gods, he became the thousand-eyed one, thunderbolt-handed and of great renown.

sanskrit: sudhāvadātaṃ raktākṣaṃ stabdhakarṇaṃ madotkaṭam āveṣṭitakaraṃ raudraṃ caturdaṃṣṭraṃ mahāgajam
english: He mounted a mighty elephant, white as nectar, with red eyes, ears held stiffly erect, fierce in its rut, its trunk coiled, terrible to behold, and armed with four tusks.

sanskrit: samāsthitaś ca bhagavān dīpyamānaḥ svatejasā ājagāma kirīṭī tu hārakeyūrabhūṣitaḥ
english: Mounted upon it, the Lord came on, blazing with his own splendour, crowned with a diadem and adorned with necklaces and armlets.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani sevyamāno 'psarobhiś ca divyagandharvanāditaḥ
english: A white parasol was held above his head, the Apsarases waited upon him, and the music of celestial Gandharvas resounded around him.

sanskrit: tato mām āha devendraḥ prītas te 'haṃ dvijottama varaṃ vṛṇīṣva mattas tvaṃ yat te manasi vartate
english: Then the lord of the gods spoke to me: 'I am pleased with you, O best of the twice-born; choose from me whatever boon dwells in your heart.'

sanskrit: śakrasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā nāhaṃ prītamanābhavam abruvaṃ ca tadā kṛṣṇa devarājam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: But hearing Śakra's words, O Kṛṣṇa, my heart was not gladdened, and I then spoke to the king of the gods these words.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tvatto varaṃ kāṅkṣe nānyasmād api daivatāt mahādevād ṛte saumya satyam etad bravīmi te
english: 'I desire no boon from you, nor from any other deity save Mahādeva, O gentle one; this truth I tell you.'

sanskrit: paśupativacanād bhavāmi sadyaḥ; kṛmir atha vā tarur apy anekaśākhaḥ apaśupativaraprasādajā me; tribhuvanarājyavibhūtir apy aniṣṭā
english: 'At a word from Paśupati I would gladly become at once a worm, or a tree with countless branches; but the sovereignty and splendour even of the three worlds, if not born of Paśupati's gracious boon, is unwelcome to me.'

sanskrit: api kīṭaḥ pataṃgo vā bhaveyaṃ śaṃkarājñayā na tu śakra tvayā dattaṃ trailokyam api kāmaye
english: 'Even an insect or a moth I would gladly become at Śaṃkara's command; but the dominion over the three worlds, were it given by you, O Śakra, I do not desire.'

sanskrit: yāvac chaśāṅkaśakalāmalabaddhamaulir; na prīyate paśupatir bhagavān mameśaḥ tāvaj jarāmaraṇajanmaśatābhighātair; duḥkhāni dehavihitāni samudvahāmi
english: 'So long as Paśupati, my Lord and God, whose locks are bound with the pure crescent fragment of the moon, is not pleased with me, so long shall I bear the sorrows ordained for the body, smitten by a hundred old ages, deaths, and births.'

sanskrit: divasakaraśaśāṅkavahnidīptaṃ; tribhuvanasāram apāram ādyam ekam ajaram amaram aprasādya rudraṃ; jagati pumān iha ko labheta śāntim
english: 'Without winning the favour of Rudra—radiant as sun, moon, and fire, the essence of the three worlds, boundless, primordial, unique, unaging, undying—what man in this world could ever attain peace?'

sanskrit: śakra uvāca kaḥ punas tava hetur vai īśe kāraṇakāraṇe yena devād ṛte 'nyasmāt prasādaṃ nābhikāṅkṣasi
english: Śakra said: 'And what is your reason concerning the Lord, the Cause of all causes, that you should seek favour from no god other than him?'

sanskrit: upamanyur uvāca hetubhir vā kim anyais te īśaḥ kāraṇakāraṇam na śuśruma yad anyasya liṅgam abhyarcyate suraiḥ
english: Upamanyu said: 'What need have you of other reasons? The Lord is the Cause of all causes. We have never heard that the emblem of any other is worshipped by the gods.'

sanskrit: kasyānyasya suraiḥ sarvair liṅgaṃ muktvā maheśvaram arcyate 'rcitapūrvaṃ vā brūhi yady asti te śrutiḥ
english: 'Whose emblem, save that of Maheśvara, is worshipped by all the gods, or has been worshipped of old? Tell me, if you have heard of any such.'

sanskrit: yasya brahmā ca viṣṇuś ca tvaṃ cāpi saha daivataiḥ arcayadhvaṃ sadā liṅgaṃ tasmāc chreṣṭhatamo hi saḥ
english: 'He whose emblem Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and you too together with the gods, forever worship—he therefore is the most supreme of all.'

sanskrit: tasmād varam ahaṃ kāṅkṣe nidhanaṃ vāpi kauśika gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā śakra yatheṣṭaṃ balasūdana
english: 'From him alone do I desire a boon, or even death itself, O Kauśika. Go or stay as you please, O Śakra, slayer of Bala.'

sanskrit: kāmam eṣa varo me 'stu śāpo vāpi maheśvarāt na cānyāṃ devatāṃ kāṅkṣe sarvakāmaphalāny api
english: 'Let it be, then—whether a boon be mine from Maheśvara, or even a curse; I desire no other deity, not though it bring me the fruit of all my wishes.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu devendraṃ duḥkhād ākulitendriyaḥ na prasīdati me rudraḥ kim etad iti cintayan athāpaśyaṃ kṣaṇenaiva tam evairāvataṃ punaḥ
english: Having thus spoken to the lord of the gods, my senses troubled with grief and brooding, 'Why is it that Rudra is not gracious to me?'—in that very instant I beheld once again that same Airāvata.

sanskrit: haṃsakundendusadṛśaṃ mṛṇālakumudaprabham vṛṣarūpadharaṃ sākṣāt kṣīrodam iva sāgaram
english: It had taken the form of a bull, like a swan, like jasmine, like the moon, gleaming as the lotus-stalk and the white water-lily, vast as the very Ocean of Milk before my eyes.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapucchaṃ mahākāyaṃ madhupiṅgalalocanam jāmbūnadena dāmnā ca sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: Huge of body, with a black tail and eyes tawny as honey, adorned on every side with a girth of pure gold.

sanskrit: raktākṣaṃ sumahānāsaṃ sukarṇaṃ sukaṭītaṭam supārśvaṃ vipulaskandhaṃ surūpaṃ cārudarśanam
english: Red-eyed, with a great muzzle, fine ears, fine flanks at the haunch, well-formed sides, broad shoulders—shapely and lovely to behold.

sanskrit: kakudaṃ tasya cābhāti skandham āpūrya viṣṭhitam tuṣāragirikūṭābhaṃ sitābhraśikharopamam
english: Its hump shone, rising full upon its shoulder, like the peak of a snow-clad mountain, like the crest of a white cloud.

sanskrit: tam āsthitaś ca bhagavān devadevaḥ sahomayā aśobhata mahādevaḥ paurṇamāsyām ivoḍurāṭ
english: Mounted upon it together with Umā, the Lord, God of gods, the great Mahādeva, shone like the lord of the stars on the night of the full moon.

sanskrit: tasya tejobhavo vahniḥ sameghaḥ stanayitnumān sahasram iva sūryāṇāṃ sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: The fire born of his radiance, charged with clouds and thunder, stood enveloping all things like a thousand suns at once.

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ sumahātejāḥ saṃvartaka ivānalaḥ yugānte sarvabhūtāni didhakṣur iva codyataḥ
english: The Lord, of vast and mighty splendour, was like the all-consuming fire, poised as if to burn up every being at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: tejasā tu tadā vyāpte durnirīkṣye samantataḥ punar udvignahṛdayaḥ kim etad iti cintayam
english: When that splendour, hard to gaze upon, had spread on every side, my heart was troubled once more, and I pondered, 'What is this?'

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tat tejo vyāpya sarvā diśo daśa praśāntaṃ ca kṣaṇenaiva devadevasya māyayā
english: That splendour, having filled all the ten directions for but a moment, was in an instant stilled again by the power of the God of gods.

sanskrit: athāpaśyaṃ sthitaṃ sthāṇuṃ bhagavantaṃ maheśvaram saurabheyagataṃ saumyaṃ vidhūmam iva pāvakam sahitaṃ cārusarvāṅgyā pārvatyā parameśvaram
english: Then I beheld the Lord Maheśvara, the Steadfast One, standing there—gentle, seated upon the bull, like a smokeless flame—the Supreme Lord together with Pārvatī, fair in every limb.

sanskrit: nīlakaṇṭhaṃ mahātmānam asaktaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim aṣṭādaśabhujaṃ sthāṇuṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam
english: The blue-throated, great-souled, unattached one, treasury of all splendours, the Steadfast, with eighteen arms, adorned with every ornament.

sanskrit: śuklāmbaradharaṃ devaṃ śuklamālyānulepanam śukladhvajam anādhṛṣyaṃ śuklayajñopavītinam
english: The God clad in white garments, garlanded and anointed in white, bearing a white banner, unassailable, wearing the white sacred thread.

sanskrit: gāyadbhir nṛtyamānaiś ca utpatadbhir itas tataḥ vṛtaṃ pāriṣadair divyair ātmatulyaparākramaiḥ
english: He was surrounded by his celestial attendants—singing, dancing, leaping here and there—each equal to himself in valour.

sanskrit: bālendumukuṭaṃ pāṇḍuṃ śaraccandram ivoditam tribhir netraiḥ kṛtoddyotaṃ tribhiḥ sūryair ivoditaiḥ
english: Crowned with the crescent moon, pale-bright as the autumn moon newly risen, blazing with his three eyes like three suns risen at once.

sanskrit: aśobhata ca devasya mālā gātre sitaprabhe jātarūpamayaiḥ padmair grathitā ratnabhūṣitā
english: And upon the God's body, fair of hue, there shone a garland woven of golden lotuses and set with jewels.

sanskrit: mūrtimanti tathāstrāṇi sarvatejomayāni ca mayā dṛṣṭāni govinda bhavasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: And the weapons of Bhava, of measureless splendour—embodied and wholly made of radiance—these I beheld, O Govinda.

sanskrit: indrāyudhasahasrābhaṃ dhanus tasya mahātmanaḥ pinākam iti vikhyātaṃ sa ca vai pannago mahān
english: The bow of that great-souled one, gleaming like a thousand rainbows, renowned by the name of Pināka—and that bow was itself a mighty serpent.

sanskrit: saptaśīrṣo mahākāyas tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro viṣolbaṇaḥ jyāveṣṭitamahāgrīvaḥ sthitaḥ puruṣavigrahaḥ
english: Seven-headed, vast of body, with sharp fangs and abounding in venom, its great neck wound about as the bowstring, it stood there in the shape of a man.

sanskrit: śaraś ca sūryasaṃkāśaḥ kālānalasamadyutiḥ yat tad astraṃ mahāghoraṃ divyaṃ pāśupataṃ mahat
english: And the arrow, resembling the sun, of a brilliance like the fire of doom—that great and most terrible divine weapon, the mighty Pāśupata.

sanskrit: advitīyam anirdeśyaṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham sasphuliṅgaṃ mahākāyaṃ visṛjantam ivānalam
english: Without a peer, beyond all describing, striking terror into every being, huge of frame and scattering sparks, as though shedding forth fire.

sanskrit: ekapādaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ sahasraśirasodaram sahasrabhujajihvākṣam udgirantam ivānalam
english: One-footed, with great fangs, with a thousand heads and bellies, with a thousand arms, tongues, and eyes, as though belching forth fire.

sanskrit: brāhmān nārāyaṇād aindrād āgneyād api vāruṇāt yad viśiṣṭaṃ mahābāho sarvaśastravighātanam
english: Surpassing the weapons of Brahmā, of Nārāyaṇa, of Indra, of Agni, and of Varuṇa, O mighty-armed one, and the destroyer of every other weapon.

sanskrit: yena tat tripuraṃ dagdhvā kṣaṇād bhasmīkṛtaṃ purā śareṇaikena govinda mahādevena līlayā
english: By which, in days of old, Mahādeva burned Tripura and reduced it to ashes in an instant, with a single arrow and as if in sport, O Govinda.

sanskrit: nirdadāha jagat kṛtsnaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram maheśvarabhujotsṛṣṭaṃ nimeṣārdhān na saṃśayaḥ
english: Loosed from Maheśvara's arm, it would consume the whole universe, the three worlds with all that moves and is unmoving, in half the blink of an eye—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: nāvadhyo yasya loke 'smin brahmaviṣṇusureṣv api tad ahaṃ dṛṣṭavāṃs tāta āścaryādbhutam uttamam
english: In this world there is none it cannot slay, not even among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the gods. That weapon, supremely wondrous and marvellous, did I behold, my friend.

sanskrit: guhyam astraṃ paraṃ cāpi tattulyādhikam eva vā yat tac chūlam iti khyātaṃ sarvalokeṣu śūlinaḥ
english: And another supreme and secret weapon, equal to it or even greater—that which is renowned throughout all the worlds as the trident of the Trident-bearer.

sanskrit: dārayed yan mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ śoṣayed vā mahodadhim saṃhared vā jagat kṛtsnaṃ visṛṣṭaṃ śūlapāṇinā
english: Hurled by the Trident-handed one, it could cleave the whole earth asunder, or dry up the great ocean, or destroy the entire universe.

sanskrit: yauvanāśvo hato yena māṃdhātā sabalaḥ purā cakravartī mahātejās trilokavijayī nṛpaḥ
english: By it, in olden times, was Māndhātṛ slain, the son of Yuvanāśva, together with his army—a sovereign emperor of vast splendour, the king who had conquered the three worlds.

sanskrit: mahābalo mahāvīryaḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ karasthenaiva govinda lavaṇasyeha rakṣasaḥ
english: Mighty in strength and valour, in prowess the equal of Śakra, he was slain, O Govinda, by that trident here held in the hand of the demon Lavaṇa.

sanskrit: tac chūlam atitīkṣṇāgraṃ subhīmaṃ lomaharṣaṇam triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā tarjamānam iva sthitam
english: That trident, exceedingly sharp of point, most dreadful and hair-raising, stood as though it had drawn its three prongs into a frown and was threatening all before it.

sanskrit: vidhūmaṃ sārciṣaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kālasūryam ivoditam sarpahastam anirdeśyaṃ pāśahastam ivāntakam dṛṣṭavān asmi govinda tad astraṃ rudrasaṃnidhau
english: Smokeless yet flaming, dark, risen like the sun of doom, serpent in hand, beyond describing, like Death with his noose in hand—that weapon I beheld, O Govinda, in the presence of Rudra.

sanskrit: paraśus tīkṣṇadhāraś ca datto rāmasya yaḥ purā mahādevena tuṣṭena kṣatriyāṇāṃ kṣayaṃkaraḥ kārtavīryo hato yena cakravartī mahāmṛdhe
english: And the keen-edged axe that of old was given to Rāma by the well-pleased Mahādeva, bringer of destruction to the Kṣatriyas—by which, in a mighty battle, the emperor Kārtavīrya was slain.

sanskrit: triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī yena niḥkṣatriyā kṛtā jāmadagnyena govinda rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: By which the earth was made bereft of Kṣatriyas thrice seven times over, O Govinda, by Rāma the son of Jamadagni, of unwearied deeds.

sanskrit: dīptadhāraḥ suraudrāsyaḥ sarpakaṇṭhāgraveṣṭitaḥ abhavac chūlino 'bhyāśe dīptavahniśikhopamaḥ
english: With blazing edge and most fearsome face, wound about at the throat and tip with serpents, it stood beside the Trident-bearer like a tongue of flaming fire.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyāni cāstrāṇi tasya divyāni dhīmataḥ prādhānyato mayaitāni kīrtitāni tavānagha
english: Numberless are the divine weapons of that wise one; these, the chief among them, have I recounted to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: savyadeśe tu devasya brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ divyaṃ vimānam āsthāya haṃsayuktaṃ manojavam
english: On the God's left side stood Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, mounted upon a celestial car yoked with swans and swift as thought.

sanskrit: vāmapārśvagataś caiva tathā nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ vainateyaṃ samāsthāya śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ
english: And likewise Nārāyaṇa stood upon his left flank, mounted upon the son of Vinatā, bearing conch, discus, and mace.

sanskrit: skando mayūram āsthāya sthito devyāḥ samīpataḥ śaktiṃ kaṇṭhe samādāya dvitīya iva pāvakaḥ
english: Skanda, mounted upon his peacock, stood near the Goddess, his spear held aslant his shoulder, like a second fire.

sanskrit: purastāc caiva devasya nandiṃ paśyāmy avasthitam śūlaṃ viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhantaṃ dvitīyam iva śaṃkaram
english: And before the God I saw Nandin stationed, standing braced upon his trident, like a second Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvādyā manavo bhṛgvādyā ṛṣayas tathā śakrādyā devatāś caiva sarva eva samabhyayuḥ
english: The Manus, beginning with Svāyaṃbhuva, the sages, beginning with Bhṛgu, and the gods, beginning with Śakra—all alike drew near.

sanskrit: te 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ parivārya samantataḥ astuvan vividhaiḥ stotrair mahādevaṃ surās tadā
english: Saluting the great-souled one and encircling him on every side, the gods then praised Mahādeva with hymns of many kinds.

sanskrit: brahmā bhavaṃ tadā stunvan rathantaram udīrayan jyeṣṭhasāmnā ca deveśaṃ jagau nārāyaṇas tadā gṛṇañ śakraḥ paraṃ brahma śatarudrīyam uttamam
english: Brahmā, praising Bhava, intoned the Rathantara hymn; and Nārāyaṇa then sang to the Lord of gods with the Jyeṣṭha Sāman; while Śakra chanted the supreme Brahman, the excellent Śatarudrīya.

sanskrit: brahmā nārāyaṇaś caiva devarājaś ca kauśikaḥ aśobhanta mahātmānas trayas traya ivāgnayaḥ
english: Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa and Kauśika the king of the gods—those three great-souled ones shone like three sacred fires.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhyagato devo rarāja bhagavāñ śivaḥ śaradghanavinirmuktaḥ pariviṣṭa ivāṃśumān tato 'ham astuvaṃ devaṃ stavenānena suvratam
english: In their midst the Lord God Śiva shone resplendent, like the sun freed from the autumn clouds yet still wreathed in a halo. Then I too praised that God of holy vows with this hymn.

sanskrit: namo devādhidevāya mahādevāya vai namaḥ śakrāya śakrarūpāya śakraveṣadharāya ca
english: Homage to the God of gods, homage indeed to Mahādeva; to Śakra, to him whose form is Śakra's, to him who wore the garb of Śakra.

sanskrit: namas te vajrahastāya piṅgalāyāruṇāya ca pinākapāṇaye nityaṃ khaḍgaśūladharāya ca
english: Homage to you, thunderbolt in hand, tawny and ruddy of hue; to the Pināka-bearer evermore, to him who bears the sword and the trident.

sanskrit: namas te kṛṣṇavāsāya kṛṣṇakuñcitamūrdhaje kṛṣṇājinottarīyāya kṛṣṇāṣṭam iratāya ca
english: Homage to you, clad in black, with dark curling locks, mantled in a black antelope hide, and delighting in the eighth of the dark fortnight.

sanskrit: śuklavarṇāya śuklāya śuklāmbaradharāya ca śuklabhasmāvaliptāya śuklakarmaratāya ca
english: To the white of hue, to the white one, to him clad in white garments, smeared with white ashes, and delighting in pure deeds.

sanskrit: tvaṃ brahmā sarvadevānāṃ rudrāṇāṃ nīlalohitaḥ ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ sāṃkhye puruṣa ucyase
english: You are Brahmā among all the gods, the blue-and-red Nīlalohita among the Rudras, the Self of all beings, and in the Sāṃkhya you are called the Puruṣa.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhas tvaṃ pavitrāṇāṃ yogināṃ niṣkalaḥ śivaḥ āśramāṇāṃ gṛhasthas tvam īśvarāṇāṃ maheśvaraḥ kuberaḥ sarvayakṣāṇāṃ kratūnāṃ viṣṇur ucyase
english: You are the bull among holy things, the partless and auspicious one among the Yogins; among the stages of life you are the householder, among lords you are Maheśvara, among all the Yakṣas you are Kubera, and among sacrifices you are called Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: parvatānāṃ mahāmerur nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca candramāḥ vasiṣṭhas tvam ṛṣīṇāṃ ca grahāṇāṃ sūrya ucyase
english: Among mountains you are the great Meru, among the lunar mansions the Moon; among the sages you are Vasiṣṭha, and among the planets you are called the Sun.

sanskrit: āraṇyānāṃ paśūnāṃ ca siṃhas tvaṃ parameśvaraḥ grāmyāṇāṃ govṛṣaś cāsi bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ
english: Among the beasts of the forest you are the lion, O Supreme Lord; among the beasts of the village you are the bull, O Lord, worshipped by all the world.

sanskrit: ādityānāṃ bhavān viṣṇur vasūnāṃ caiva pāvakaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ vainateyaś ca ananto bhujageṣu ca
english: Among the Ādityas you are Viṣṇu, among the Vasus the Fire-god, among birds the son of Vinatā, and among serpents you are Ananta.

sanskrit: sāmavedaś ca vedānāṃ yajuṣāṃ śatarudriyam sanatkumāro yogīnāṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ kapilo hy asi
english: Among the Vedas you are the Sāmaveda, among the Yajus formulas the Śatarudrīya, among the Yogins Sanatkumāra, and among the followers of Sāṃkhya you are Kapila.

sanskrit: śakro 'si marutāṃ deva pitṝṇāṃ dharmarāḍ asi brahmalokaś ca lokānāṃ gatīnāṃ mokṣa ucyase
english: Among the Maruts you are Śakra, O God; among the ancestral fathers you are the king of dharma; among the worlds you are the world of Brahmā, and among the goals you are called liberation.

sanskrit: kṣīrodaḥ sāgarāṇāṃ ca śailānāṃ himavān giriḥ varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇaś cāsi viprāṇāṃ dīkṣito dvijaḥ ādis tvam asi lokānāṃ saṃhartā kāla eva ca
english: Among the oceans you are the Ocean of Milk, among mountains the Himavat; among the social orders you are the Brāhmaṇa, and among the learned the consecrated twice-born. You are the beginning of the worlds, and you are likewise their destroyer, even Time itself.

sanskrit: yac cānyad api lokeṣu sattvaṃ tejodhikaṃ smṛtam tat sarvaṃ bhagavān eva iti me niścitā matiḥ
english: And whatever other being in the worlds is held to surpass the rest in splendour—all that is the Lord himself: such is my settled conviction.

sanskrit: namas te bhagavan deva namas te bhaktavatsala yogeśvara namas te 'stu namas te viśvasaṃbhava
english: Homage to you, O Lord and God; homage to you, tender to your devotees; homage be to you, O Lord of Yoga; homage to you, O source of the universe.
